headline.title: Announcing our $160M grant from Coefficient Giving
headline.summary: Resolution (formerly Sequent) has received a $160 million grant from Coefficient Giving to enhance alignment research in AI. The funding, which includes a $108 million base and $52 million contingent on hiring and compute requirements, aims to advance understanding of AI alignment challenges.

articles.title: Lovable reportedly in talks to double its valuation to $13.2B
articles.summary: Lovable is reportedly in discussions to secure a $300 million funding round that could double its valuation to $13.2 billion, with Menlo Ventures expected to lead the investment. This development follows ongoing interest in the company's growth and market potential.

articles.title: Cost-Effective Agent Harnesses for Abstract Reasoning and Generalization on ARC-AGI-1
articles.summary: A new study explores a cost-effective approach to abstract reasoning and generalization using the DeepSeek V3.2 model on the ARC-AGI-1 benchmark, focusing on an open-weight model in non-thinking mode without extensive computational resources. This method contrasts with previous strategies that relied on heavy test-time computation or benchmark-specific training.

articles.title: D2PO: Optimizing Diffusion Samplers via Dynamic Preference
articles.summary: The article introduces D2PO (Dynamic Direct Preference Optimization), a framework designed to enhance diffusion sampling policies by optimizing timestep schedules and classifier-free guidance weights. This approach addresses limitations in current student-teacher regression frameworks, particularly the trade-off between high-frequency texture fidelity and global coherence in low-NFE student samplers.

articles.title: Inertia-1: An Open Exploration of Wearable Motion Foundation Models
articles.summary: Inertia-1 is a newly introduced open exploration of wearable motion foundation models aimed at enhancing understanding of human behavior and health through continuous motion sensing. The study addresses the limitations of previous research by examining diverse real-world sensing scenarios rather than isolated design choices.

articles.title: Overview of the NLPCC 2026 Shared Task 1: Difficulty-Aware Multilingual and Multimodal Medical Instructional Video Understanding Evaluation
articles.summary: The NLPCC 2026 will feature the Difficulty-Aware Medical Instructional Video Question Answering (DA-MIVQA) shared task, which builds on prior challenges by categorizing questions based on the complexity of evidence needed for answers. This initiative aims to enhance multilingual and multimodal benchmarks in medical video understanding.

articles.title: SpaR3D-MoE: Adaptive 3D Spatial Reasoning from Sparse Views Meets Geometry-Inductive Mixture-of-Experts
articles.summary: The article introduces SpaR3D-MoE, a novel approach designed to enhance 3D spatial reasoning from sparse views by integrating a geometry-inductive mixture-of-experts framework. This method aims to address the limitations of current multimodal large language models in effectively connecting 2D semantic understanding with 3D spatial geometry without relying on expensive 3D data.

articles.title: Digital Fragmentation and Generative AI Use Across 103 Million Application Events
articles.summary: A study analyzing 103 million application events from 1,017 employees reveals that knowledge workers frequently switch between digital applications, spending nearly 10% of their work year on these transitions, a phenomenon termed digital fragmentation. The research aims to understand the implications of this fragmentation in relation to employee identity, work environment, and daily experiences.

articles.title: From Agentic to Autogenic Network Management for AI-Native 6G and Beyond: A Standards Perspective
articles.summary: Standards bodies such as TM Forum, 3GPP, and ETSI are focusing on Agentic AI for the management of next-generation 6G networks, utilizing Large AI Model-based agents for autonomous resource coordination and operational adaptation. To effectively implement this vision, there is a need for management systems capable of generating and evolving their own automation software to handle the complexity of 6G networks.

articles.title: A Multi-Analyst LLM Pipeline for Auditable Rule Discovery Across 68 Public Physiological Corpora
articles.summary: A new study presents a controlled workflow utilizing a four-analyst large-language model (LLM) to analyze 68 public physiological corpora, addressing their heterogeneity in sensors, labels, and recording settings. The approach aims to facilitate auditable rule discovery for detector design in contactless monitoring platforms.

articles.title: Memory Scarcity, Open Models, and the Restructuring of the AI Industry, 2026-2030 -- A quantitative scenario analysis of inference economics, training-cost divergence, and infrastructure solvency
articles.summary: The article presents a quantitative scenario analysis of the AI industry from 2026 to 2030, focusing on the impacts of DRAM/HBM price increases, the emergence of open-weight models, advancements in inference efficiency, and the entry of new players like Meta and xAI in compute resale. It formulates inference economics in terms of cost per petabyte of bandwidth delivered, highlighting the potential restructuring of the industry due to these factors.

articles.title: HAJJv2-CrowdCount: Zero-Shot Benchmark for Dense Crowd Counting
articles.summary: The article introduces HAJJv2-CrowdCount, a new zero-shot benchmark designed for evaluating dense crowd counting in Hajj video footage, which presents unique challenges due to steep camera angles and extensive occlusion. This benchmark aims to address the limitations of existing models and provide a detailed assessment of crowd counting performance in such complex environments.
